pages.scan: Wide top panel: caption top-left 'A busy day at Dr. Ananya's clinic.' with a small ananya face box in the centre (silent establishing shot). Bottom-left panel: meera balloon at top-left 'Appointments, patient details, follow-ups...', then a meera balloon below her face 'I wish everything were easier to manage!'. Bottom-right panel: ananya balloon at top 'Our time belongs with patients. Let's make the rest simpler.'
pages.observation: Risk of skipping a line: Ananya's reply balloon in the right panel sits at the same height as Meera's first balloon. Meera's second balloon ('I wish...') is much lower, under her face. A reader on the top line of this tier can go straight from 'Appointments...' across to 'Our time belongs...' and only then drop back to 'I wish...', so the reply comes before the complaint it answers. Raise Meera's second balloon or lower Ananya's balloon. Meera has no role or introduction (the caption only names Dr. Ananya). Ananya and Meera are in separate panels, so it is unclear whether they share a room. The tall bottom-left panel has a lot of empty space below the second balloon. Panel 1 has a small face and no action, so the 'busy' in the caption has to come from the art.

pages.scan: Top panel with no face boxes: caption top-left 'The clinic begins its Welbuk onboarding.' and teal label top-right 'WELBUK PRACTICE for the clinic'. Middle-left: ananya 'We can organise our clinic workflow here.' Middle-right: meera 'And our team can use tools suited to each staff role.', teal label bottom 'WELBUK CARE for clinic staff'. Bottom wide panel: ananya 'One team. Better coordination.' with meera beside her, silent.
pages.observation: The order reads cleanly: caption, label, Ananya, Meera, label, Ananya. Meera's 'And...' follows on naturally from Ananya. Ananya's 'here' has nothing to point at: the panel shows no screen or device, and the panel before it has no people or object. The art must show the Welbuk interface or Ananya gesturing at it. Panel 1 is a wide panel with no faces, carried only by caption and label. In the last panel Meera is silent; her reaction (nod or smile) has to be drawn or her presence means nothing. Ananya's middle-left tail is a long diagonal across empty space, but it reaches her.

pages.scan: Top-left: ravi 'Good morning! I'd like to see the doctor.' Top-right: meera 'Of course. May I register your details for today's appointment?' Middle wide: ravi left 'Yes, please.', meera right silent. Bottom wide: meera right 'You're all set, Ravi. Please have a seat.', ravi left silent.
pages.observation: The question and answer order is unambiguous, and Ravi left / Meera right holds across panels 3-4. Time jump: the registration itself (details given, typed in) is never shown between 'Yes, please.' and 'You're all set'. Meera calls him 'Ravi' although he never gives his name on the page. Both only work if the art shows her registering him on a screen, or a beat panel is added. Nothing on the page establishes the setting as a reception desk. In the last panel Ravi is silent; his reaction to being sent to sit is not specified.

pages.scan: Top wide: ananya left 'Hello, Ravi. Tell me what brings you in.', ravi right silent. Middle-left: ravi 'I've been feeling tired lately.' Middle-right: caption 'Technology supports the workflow. The conversation stays human.' over a silent ananya. Bottom wide: ananya left 'We'll go through your concerns and decide the right next steps together.', ravi right silent.
pages.observation: There is no caption marking the move from reception to the consultation room; the reader only infers it from Ananya's greeting. The narration caption sits between Ravi's complaint and Ananya's reply, where her direct response to 'tired' would go. Her bottom line then answers in general terms ('your concerns'), so the tiredness is never picked up and the exchange feels cut off. 'Technology' in the caption has no visible referent in any panel. Ananya left / Ravi right is consistent in the wide panels. In the middle-right panel Ananya has no balloon, so her listening expression carries the beat.

pages.scan: Top wide: meera left 'Welbuk Health is designed to help patients stay connected with their care.', ravi right silent. Middle-left: ravi 'So I can keep useful information in one place?', teal label bottom-left 'WELBUK HEALTH for patients'. Middle-right: meera 'That's the idea. Let's walk through what is available to you.' Bottom wide: caption 'A smoother visit. A more connected experience.' over ravi alone, silent.
pages.observation: Another change of location and partner with no transition: page 4 ended with Ananya, and here Meera is talking to Ravi with no caption saying it is after the consultation or back at the desk. Ravi's 'useful information in one place' goes beyond what Meera said ('stay connected with their care'). It reads as a paraphrase, but 'useful information' is not set up. Meera promises 'Let's walk through what is available', then the page cuts straight to a summary caption, so the promised walkthrough is skipped. The label in the bottom-left of Ravi's panel is read after his question, which is fine. The final panel needs a visible reaction from Ravi to make the caption feel earned.

pages.scan: Top-left: caption 'Tomorrow, care may take us beyond our hometown.' with ravi silent. Top-right: teal label 'WELBUK VISION' and caption 'The vision: trusted connections between clinics, specialists, and patients across locations.' with a silent specialist at lower right. Middle wide: teal label 'WELBUK VISION' again and caption 'One connected ecosystem for care and family wellness.' with ravi, partner, child silent. Bottom wide: teal label 'Welbuk Practice • Welbuk Care • Welbuk Health' at top; meera, ananya, ravi silent in the centre; caption at bottom 'Welbuk — Building a connected healthcare ecosystem.'
pages.observation: The page has no dialogue, only captions and labels. The speaker of 'us' and 'our hometown' is unclear (Ravi? the clinic? a narrator?). The shift to 'Tomorrow' does not say whether these panels are imagined, the future, or the present. The specialist, partner and child appear with no introduction; nothing shows they are Ravi's family or that the specialist is remote. 'WELBUK VISION' appears in two panels in a row, and 'The vision:' repeats the label, which is redundant. The specialist face box is tight against the lower-right corner of the caption. In the last panel the order is label, then faces, then the bottom caption, which reads fine. The three faces are evenly spaced with no interaction set up, so the art has to give them shared acting.
